text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are good at tasks like summarising texts, answering questions and translating languages. However, they have limits: they can make mistakes, give outdated information, or produce false facts. They also cannot truly understand meaning the way humans do. For these reasons, it is important to check their answers carefully.
